open_points.subject: administrator project scope
open_points.text: State 0 invariant 2 says project-scoped access requires "project grant/assignment", while M07 says "administrators cover all projects through that area policy" and authorization "never consults assignments for the administrator role".
open_points.question: May an administrator perform project-scoped operations without a StaffProjectAssignment?
options: Yes; the single-area administrator policy supplies project access without assignments.
No; every staff principal, including an administrator, needs an active assignment to the project.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the more specific M07 rule as controlling and allow administrators without assignments.

witness.initial: An active administrator has no assignment to active project P.
outcomes: M07 permits the read because administrators cover every project in the single administrative area.
State 0 invariant 2 denies the read because no project assignment exists.

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal disablement lifecycle
open_points.text: Meaning says "the only modification is the status change `active ↔ disabled`", but Lifecycle candidate says "`active → disabled`".
open_points.question: Can a disabled ServicePrincipal be returned to active status?
options: Yes; disablement is reversible.
No; disabled is terminal.
open_points.default_guess: Allow re-enabling because the detailed Meaning explicitly uses a bidirectional transition.

witness.initial: A ServicePrincipal is active and then disabled; all its credentials are revoked.
events: An administrator attempts to change the principal back to active.
outcomes: The principal becomes active and can receive a new credential.
The action is refused because disabled is terminal.

open_points.subject: reactivation of a deactivated BudgetVersion
open_points.text: The lifecycle is written as "`inactive → active → inactive`" and says deactivated versions are never deleted, but it does not say whether the final inactive state may transition to active again.
open_points.question: May staff reactivate a previously deactivated BudgetVersion?
options: Yes; any retained inactive version may be activated again.
No; once a version has been deactivated, that version can never become active again.
open_points.default_guess: Allow reactivation because status has only inactive and active values and activation is described for a version without excluding previously active versions.

witness.initial: Project P has version V1 active; activating V2 deactivates V1.
events: An operator later activates V1 again.
outcomes: V1 becomes active and V2 is deactivated atomically.
The action is refused because V1's deactivation is terminal.
witness.observer: Staff and viewers reading P's budget

open_points.subject: creation of the manual BudgetVersion
open_points.text: M22 says there is "at most one manual version per project" and M21 says a "manual plan upsert without a `section_id` creates" a section, but no text says whether that upsert also creates the project's manual BudgetVersion or which other product action creates it.
open_points.question: Which product action creates the first manual BudgetVersion for a project?
options: The first manual-section upsert creates the manual BudgetVersion implicitly.
A distinct budget-creation action must create the manual BudgetVersion before sections can be upserted.
open_points.default_guess: Create the manual BudgetVersion implicitly on the first manual-section upsert.

witness.initial: Active project P has no BudgetVersion.
events: An assigned operator submits the first manual section plan for P.
outcomes: The operation creates a manual BudgetVersion, PortalSection, and SectionPlan.
The operation is refused until a separate manual-budget creation action has run.

open_points.subject: intake fingerprint after expense correction
open_points.text: The model stores `intake_fingerprint`, says corrections may change supplier, date, amount and allocations, and classifies later intake replay by fingerprint, but never says whether a correction preserves or recomputes the stored fingerprint.
open_points.question: Does correcting an Expense change its `intake_fingerprint`?
options: No; it permanently records the originally accepted intake content.
Yes; it is recomputed from the corrected expense and replacement allocations.
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the original intake fingerprint as immutable intake provenance.

witness.initial: An intake creates expense E with fingerprint F; staff then correct E's amount and allocations.
events: The original intake is submitted again with fingerprint F.
outcomes: It is an equal replay and returns the existing, now-corrected expense.
It is an integrity conflict because E's stored fingerprint was recomputed after correction.
witness.observer: The staff caller retrying the intake

open_points.subject: same intake_id with different photo content
open_points.text: The only replay rule is "replay of one `intake_id` never duplicates"; unlike Expense and WorkPayment, the text does not say how a repeated `intake_id` with different `file_ref`, date, section, caption, or visibility is classified.
open_points.question: What does publication do when an existing `intake_id` is submitted with different content?
options: Return the existing ProgressPhoto as a replay regardless of differing content.
Reject it as an integrity conflict and change nothing.
Treat the request as an edit of the existing ProgressPhoto.
open_points.default_guess: Reject different content as an integrity conflict and change nothing.

witness.initial: Photo A was published with intake_id I, file F1 and caption C1.
events: Staff publishes intake_id I again with file F2 and caption C2.
outcomes: The existing photo is returned unchanged as a replay.
The request is rejected as a conflicting reuse of I.
The existing photo is changed to F2/C2.
witness.observer: The staff caller and viewers of the gallery

open_points.subject: first-administrator bootstrap audit
open_points.text: State 0 R0-07 says the bootstrap command is "never printed, logged or audited", while M36 says it "writes one `staff.create` record with actor kind `system`".
open_points.question: Does successful first-administrator bootstrap create an AuditRecord?
options: No; bootstrap is expressly unaudited.
Yes; it creates exactly one system-authored `staff.create` AuditRecord.
open_points.default_guess: Follow State 0 R0-07 and create no AuditRecord.

witness.initial: The deployment contains no staff accounts.
events: The host operator successfully runs the local bootstrap command.
outcomes: One active administrator is created and no audit record exists.
One active administrator and one system-authored `staff.create` AuditRecord are created.
witness.observer: A later administrator or auditor inspecting audit history

open_points.subject: audit of unauthenticated snapshot-import attempts
open_points.text: M36 says "every significant action writes exactly one record" and explicitly includes "snapshot import", with `result` supporting `rejected`; State 0 R0-25 says an attempt whose bearer credential fails authentication "is recorded nowhere".
open_points.question: Does a snapshot-import request with a failing bearer credential create a rejected AuditRecord?
options: No; authentication failure is recorded nowhere.
Yes; every rejected snapshot-import action creates one AuditRecord.
open_points.default_guess: Create no record, following the explicit R0-25 authentication-failure rule.

witness.initial: A request carries an invalid producer bearer credential.
events: The caller submits a syntactically valid snapshot publication.
outcomes: Authentication is rejected and neither SnapshotImportRecord nor AuditRecord is written.
Authentication is rejected and a rejected AuditRecord is written, although no authenticated service actor is available.

open_points.subject: replay outcome placement
open_points.text: Meaning defines `ExpenseAggregate` with `replayed: bool`, while Carried changes says "the aggregate no longer carries `replayed`; the replay outcome travels in a separate operation outcome beside the aggregate" and also says "The Meaning above is the text of 2026-07-19."
open_points.question: Is `replayed` a field of ExpenseAggregate or only a field of ExpenseOperationOutcome?
options: ExpenseAggregate contains `replayed`.
ExpenseAggregate has only expense, allocations and document; ExpenseOperationOutcome carries `replayed` separately.
open_points.default_guess: Use the carried accepted-spec change: keep `replayed` only in ExpenseOperationOutcome.

witness.initial: An existing expense is returned after an equal-fingerprint intake replay.
events: The expense operation constructs its result.
outcomes: The returned ExpenseAggregate itself has `replayed=true`.
The ExpenseAggregate has no replay field and is wrapped beside `replayed=true` in ExpenseOperationOutcome.

open_points.subject: ProjectOverview project availability shape
open_points.text: ProjectOverview initially requires `project: ProjectContext`, but "Changes the accepted Factory spec made to the projections" says project context "is absent when Registry cannot be read, and a `project_availability` says so".
open_points.question: What is the final ProjectOverview shape for its project component?
options: `project` is always required and a Registry failure prevents a ProjectOverview result.
Add `project_availability`; require `project` only when that availability is `available`.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the accepted-spec change and add the availability/optional-project pair.

witness.initial: The portal has local data for project P, but Registry is temporarily unavailable.
events: An authorized caller requests P's overview.
outcomes: No ProjectOverview can be returned because its required `project` field cannot be populated.
A ProjectOverview is returned with `project_availability=temporarily_unavailable`, no project context, and independently available local components.

open_points.subject: BinaryPayload download_name presence
open_points.text: BinaryPayload declares `download_name: str | None`, while the accepted-spec changes say "`download_name` is always present".
open_points.question: Is `BinaryPayload.download_name` optional or required?
options: Optional; storage may return no download name.
Required; it is always derived from object kind and id.
open_points.default_guess: Make it required and always derive it, following R0-12 and the accepted-spec change.

witness.initial: An authorized caller requests an existing ExpenseDocument binary.
events: The storage boundary returns its BinaryPayload.
outcomes: The payload may contain `download_name=None`.
The payload must contain a derived document-and-id download name.
witness.observer: The API handler and downloading client

open_points.subject: issuing access after ClientViewer revocation
open_points.text: M01 says viewer revocation is terminal and "invalidates all viewer sessions and credentials", while M02 says administrators issue and re-issue credentials but gives no target-viewer status precondition.
open_points.question: Can an administrator issue or re-issue a ViewerAccessCredential for a revoked ClientViewer?
options: No; credential issuance requires an active viewer.
Yes; a credential record and secret may be issued, but authentication can never succeed while the viewer remains revoked.
open_points.default_guess: Reject issuance for a revoked viewer.

witness.initial: Viewer V has been revoked, and all prior credentials and sessions are revoked.
events: An administrator requests a new access link for V.
outcomes: The request is refused and no credential is minted.
A fresh credential and one-time secret are minted, but using the link cannot open an active session.
witness.observer: The administrator receiving the issuance response

open_points.subject: progress updates for sections outside the active work plan
open_points.text: M32 says only sections with planned work in the active version participate in derived progress, but says a record is created by the first update "of a section" without saying whether the section must have a work plan in the active BudgetVersion.
open_points.question: May staff create or update SectionProgress for a project section that has no planned work entry in the active budget version?
options: Yes; the record is accepted but omitted from current derived progress until the section participates in an active work plan.
No; progress updates require a section with planned work in the active budget version.
open_points.default_guess: Require the section to have a plan with positive planned work in the active version.

witness.initial: Section S belongs to project P but is absent from P's active BudgetVersion, or its active plan has zero work_planned.
events: An assigned operator sets S to 50% completion.
outcomes: A SectionProgress record is created but does not affect the current ProgressView.
The operation is refused because S does not currently participate in planned work.
witness.observer: The operator and later readers after S enters an active budget
